linguistic_propositions.proposition: The agent noun of an augmented verb is produced by replacing the imperfect subject prefix with a mim carrying damma and setting kasra on the radical before the last.
Every augmented agent noun opens with a prefixed mim vocalized with damma, whatever the form class.
Each augmented form maps to exactly one agent-noun template, so form class alone determines the shape.
When the last radical is weak the indefinite agent noun surfaces without that radical and carries tanwin kasra.
An agent noun used with verbal force may take an accusative direct object.
Participles of hollow and geminate roots are presented as plain instances of the sound template, with the medial-weak and gemination adjustments left unstated.
Many augmented agent nouns have lexicalized as profession and role nouns, which the lesson treats as a use rather than a separate derivation.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The quality adjective denotes a lasting attribute of its referent, whereas the agent noun denotes an action underway or an occupation.
فَعيل is the dominant template for stable qualities of persons, places and things.
The feminine of the فَعْلان template is formed by a distinct shape, not by adding taa marbuta.
The colour-and-defect template forms its feminine by dropping the initial augment and taking a long-alif ending, and its plural by a short-vowel shape.
The فَعْلان and أَفْعَل templates are barred from tanwin and from the genitive kasra.
Class membership is decided semantically rather than by template, because the same templates also serve other classes.

The lesson admits فاعِل-template words into the quality-adjective class, which conflicts with its own statement that that template signals ongoing action, and with the stricter traditional restriction of the class to verbs of quality.

The lesson states in one place that فَعْلان encodes a state felt as permanent and in another that it encodes a state holding right now, with فَعِل carrying the dispositional reading; the two statements are not reconciled.
فَعول is listed both as a variant of the فَعيل group and as a separate template in the reference grid.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Intensive templates express habitual, professional or excessive performance of the action named by the root, in contrast with the plain agent noun.
The doubled-middle-radical template is the most productive member of the class.
The final taa on one intensive template adds emphasis and does not mark feminine gender, so such forms describe males.
A فَعيل-shaped word belongs to the intensive class rather than the quality-adjective class when an underlying verb with an object can be recovered.
When an intensive form is annexed to a following noun, that noun corresponds to the direct object of the source verb.
The mim-initial intensive template carries a nuance of excess.
The فُعَلة template is rare, mostly scriptural, and skewed towards censured habits.
The classical restriction of the intensive templates to transitive triliteral verbs is not stated, and the six-template inventory offered here is one of several competing groupings.
The mim-initial intensive template is identical in shape to the instrument template taught later in the module, and the collision is not flagged.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The verbal noun names the action itself, stripped of agent and tense.
Bare-triliteral verbal nouns cannot be predicted from the verb template and must be learned lexically.
Semantic classes correlate with particular templates: motion with one, emotional state with another, craft with a third, physical act with a fourth.
Adding taa marbuta to the short verbal-noun template yields a noun denoting a single occurrence of the action.

When the base verbal noun already ends in taa, singularity is expressed by a following quantifying word instead of a further taa.
The verbal noun takes the article, tanwin and annexation and can occupy subject or object position.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Each augmented form has a fixed verbal-noun template, so the verbal noun follows from the form class alone.
The third form admits two verbal-noun templates; the shorter is preferred for abstract concepts and the mim-initial one for specific acts.
A weak final radical converts the second form's template to a taa-final shape, the third form's mim-initial template to a long-alif-final shape, and the fourth form's template to a hamza-final shape.
The seventh, eighth, ninth and tenth forms take kasra on the radical that follows the prefix complex.
A verbal noun's form class can be recovered from its prefix and syllable shape.
The fifth and sixth form verbal nouns differ from their verbs only in the final vowel.

Predictability is stated without exception, although lexicalized deviations exist and one appears inside the lesson itself.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The instrument noun names the tool used to perform the action of its root.
All three classical instrument templates carry kasra on the prefixed mim.
Which of the three templates a root takes is not predictable and must be learned lexically.
Each template tends towards a kind of tool: simple implements, elaborate devices, and handheld domestic items respectively.
The modern doubled-radical machine template is not a classical instrument template but fills the same function and is highly productive today.
The prefix vowel separates instrument nouns from place and time nouns.
Some roots are attested with two different instrument templates carrying the same sense.
The classical restriction of instrument nouns to transitive triliteral verbs is not stated, and several listed items are derived from augmented or hollow verbs.
One item appears under the short template in the pattern grid but under the long-alif template in the vocabulary and the paradigm of the same lesson.
The long-alif instrument template is identical in shape to the intensive adjective template taught earlier in this module, and the collision is not flagged.

proposed_new_units.summary: Decision table for mim-initial nouns, separating agent noun, patient noun, third-form verbal noun, place or time noun and instrument noun, keyed on prefix vowel, internal vowel, form class of the source verb and available vocalization, with an explicit undecidable outcome for unvocalized input.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: the ambiguity spans u-s03, u-s04 and u-s05 at once, so no single existing unit can own it; each of those units states its own template correctly while none records which competing readings must be excluded before a mim-initial token can be classified.
